extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (LEAs, IHEs, libraries, museums), Title IX Coordinators, school administrators, policy makers, and stakeholders (advocates, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble and Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) describing the Department's final Title IX regulations: scope of sex discrimination, obligations of recipients (grievance procedures, notification, training, supportive measures, pregnancy/lactation accommodations), costs/benefits, and legal/regulatory justifications. Intended to guide recipient implementation and OMB review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lactation space requirement (§106.40(b)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide an appropriate space for lactation for students and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Space must be private and clean, and not a bathroom; there is no requirement that a lactation space be a particular size, shape, or include features other than being private and clean, and not a bathroom. Spaces do not need to be designated 24 hours a day. Recipients are not required to make any particular facility changes or provide a precise number of spaces; compliance can likely be achieved using existing space at minimal/de minimis cost. Retrofitting (e.g., keypad locks or a chair) would have minimal cost. The de minimis costs are outweighed by benefits of allowing persons who are lactating to remain in school or employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable modifications for pregnancy-related conditions (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require recipients to provide reasonable modifications only to students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not required to provide such reasonable modifications to partners, family members, or others not pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions. The Department did not analyze costs of modifications not imposed by the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirements (§106.40(b)(2) and (b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must meet notification requirements to inform students of their rights under the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs associated with notification are included in the RIA. The cost of an employee or Title IX Coordinator informing a student of their rights is considered de minimis and is part of the Title IX Coordinator's duties. Training costs to support employee actions required under these provisions are discussed with training requirements under §106.40(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: No obligation to provide abortion-related benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 106.40 and 106.57(e) do not require a recipient to provide or pay for any benefit or service related to abortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters' concerns about abortion-related costs are unfounded because the regulations do not impose such requirements. See discussion of definition of 'pregnancy or related conditions' in §106.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Sex Discrimination (§106.10) — inclusion of gender identity and other bases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department clarifies the scope of Title IX to include discrimination based on gender identity, sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, sexual orientation, pregnancy or related conditions, and hostile environment sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although clarifying scope could increase costs (e.g., more investigations), the Department finds the non-monetary benefits of providing clarity and fulfilling Title IX's broad protections justify associated costs. The Department estimates inclusion may result in a 10 percent increase in investigations annually. Recipients must not carry out otherwise permissible different treatment or separation on the basis of sex in a way that would cause more than de minimis harm, including policies/practices that prevent participation consistent with gender identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of menstruation or related conditions within Title IX
rubrics_metrics.description: Menstruation or related conditions are included within the scope of Title IX as defined in §106.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying this inclusion may marginally increase costs for some recipients that limited application to 2020 amendments, but benefits justify costs. The regulations do not require recipients to provide menstrual products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption treatment (§106.12 and §106.6(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: No proposed changes to §106.12; final regulations do not alter assurances previously received by OCR. Religious institutions are not required to seek assurance of a religious exemption before asserting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations address conduct (sex discrimination), not religious beliefs; nothing requires religious students or employees to change beliefs. §106.6(d) explicitly states the regulations do not require restricting First Amendment or other constitutional rights. The Department must act in accordance with the Constitution; separate legal frameworks (e.g., Title IV of Civil Rights Act) prohibit discrimination based on religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Impact Analysis principles (EO 12866 and EO 13563)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RIA follows Executive Orders requiring OMB review and that agencies propose/adopt regulations only when benefits justify costs and that regulations be tailored and maximize net benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant principles include: (1) benefits justify costs (acknowledging some nonquantifiable benefits/costs); (2) tailor regulations to impose the least burden consistent with objectives and consider cumulative regulations; (3) choose approaches that maximize net benefits including distributive impacts and equity; (4) specify performance objectives rather than prescriptive behavior when feasible; (5) identify and assess alternatives to direct regulation (economic incentives, information). Agencies must use best available techniques to quantify benefits and costs and identify changing future compliance costs from innovation or behavioral changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for regulatory action (rationale for amending Title IX regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department determined changes were necessary to ensure regulatory framework aligns with Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination, based on Executive Orders, case law, enforcement experience, and stakeholder feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder input included the June 2021 Title IX Public Hearing (280+ live comments, 30,000+ written comments) and listening sessions covering survivors, accused students, LGBTQI+ students, advocates, administrators, attorneys, State AGs, Title IX Coordinators, trainers, campus law enforcement, etc. Changes aim to improve educational environments free of sex discrimination while recognizing fairness and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to adopt grievance procedures providing prompt and equitable resolution (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt grievance procedures that provide for the prompt and equitable resolution of complaints of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures must take necessary steps to provide an educational environment free from sex discrimination and allow recipients to adapt procedures to size, population served, and administrative structure while ensuring equitable treatment of all parties. Changes intend to reduce administrative burden from overly adversarial processes while ensuring fairness and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient obligation to respond promptly and effectively upon knowledge (§106.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient with knowledge of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination in its education program or activity must respond promptly and effectively, regardless of whether a complaint is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44 expands coverage beyond the 2020 amendments (which focused on allegations of sexual harassment reported to certain employees). The prescribed actions should aid recipients in reducing sex discrimination; initial short-term costs are expected to be minimal and offset by long-term reductions in discrimination. The Department cannot firmly quantify reductions in incidents but expects deterrence and prevention effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement and Title IX Coordinator role (§106.44(f)(1)(ii) and (g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon notification of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, a Title IX Coordinator must offer and coordinate supportive measures as appropriate to complainants and respondents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.44(g) clarifies that for allegations other than sex-based harassment or retaliation, provision of supportive measures does not require altering the alleged discriminatory conduct. Supportive measures also cover prohibited retaliation and other sex discrimination forms; the number of incidents seeking supportive measures may increase, and those costs are included in the Department's model. Eliminating the source of discrimination is typically a remedy, not a supportive measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator monitoring duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators must monitor the recipient's education program or activity for barriers to reporting sex discrimination and take steps reasonably calculated to address those barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This monitoring is part of the recipient's obligation to take action to address sex discrimination and is expected to improve reporting and equitable resolution. Associated costs are considered in training and Coordinator duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirements — expanded and specified audience (§106.40(d) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations modify and strengthen training requirements by specifying the range of persons a recipient must train regarding obligations under Title IX and this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training costs (initial and ongoing) are included in the RIA and are part of implementing notification and employee actions under §106.40(b). The Department anticipates training will improve responsiveness and compliance while imposing some initial costs that may be offset over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification duty for specific employees to inform Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations revise notification requirements to help ensure that specific employees notify the Title IX Coordinator when they have information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is intended to improve timely identification of incidents and coordination of supportive measures and responses; the cost of such notifications is considered de minimis and part of Coordinator duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies obligation when discrimination is found
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient determines that sex discrimination has occurred, it must provide remedies, as appropriate, to a complainant and any person identified as having their equal access limited or denied by sex discrimination, and take other appropriate prompt and effective steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies may include eliminating the source of discrimination and other steps beyond supportive measures. The obligation helps ensure redress and prevention of recurrence; costs and forms of remedies may vary by recipient and are considered in the broader RIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing baseline and limitations — data constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department must establish a baseline for estimating costs/benefits but acknowledges limited quantitative data on current recipient practices, especially at LEA level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to variation among recipients and limited status-quo data, precise estimation is not possible. The Department relied on best available evidence and modeling assumptions (e.g., estimate of a 10 percent increase in investigations) to produce NPV and annualized cost estimates. Year 1 includes one-time policy/training changes; Years 2–10 include savings from flexibility in grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost–benefit conclusion (RIA outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department determined that benefits of the final regulations justify their costs and that the regulatory action is 'significant' under EO 12866 (section 3(f)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RIA estimates net costs (e.g., NPV $18.8M at 7%; $4.636M at 3% discount) and annualized costs; Year 1 higher due to one-time implementation costs with subsequent annual cost savings. The Department emphasizes non-monetary benefits that are difficult to quantify but substantial — reducing prevalence of sex discrimination and its harms.
